info.title: Altinn PDP REST API
info.description:
Asks Altinn whether a system user or a person may perform an action on an Altinn resource, on behalf of an
organisation.

The token your API receives says who the caller is. It does not say whether they have access to your
resource. That is what this API answers.

## How to use it

1. Validate the token your API received, as you do today. This API never sees that token.
2. Take the subject and the organisation from the token. For a system user (Maskinporten token), send
   `systemuserId`. For a person (Ansattporten token), send `pid`. Either way, also send
   `customerOrganizationNumber`.
3. Call `POST /authorize` with those, your `resourceId` and the `action`.
4. Grant access only if `permit` is `true` and your end user meets `minimumAuthenticationLevel`, when the
   response has one.
5. Treat everything else as no access, including every error response.

Set your client timeout to at least 10 seconds. If Altinn is slow, you then get a `502` instead of a
timeout of your own.

## Authentication level

A `PERMIT` can come with a `minimumAuthenticationLevel`. The permit then only holds if your end user logged
in at that level or higher. This API cannot check that, so you must. Your user's level is:

| End user | Level |
| :-- | :-- |
| A system user, or any other Maskinporten token | 3 |
| A person whose Ansattporten token has `acr` `substantial` | 3 |
| A person whose Ansattporten token has `acr` `high` | 4 |

If your user's level is lower than `minimumAuthenticationLevel`, treat the answer as no access.

## How fresh the answer is

This API may answer from a cache instead of asking Altinn every time. A cached answer can still say `PERMIT`
for a while after the access was removed in Altinn.

Send `Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>` to say how old an answer you accept. Send `max-age=0`, or `no-cache`,
when you need Altinn's answer right now, for example before a write. Without the header, the server's default
applies. The server also has an upper limit, and never answers with anything older, whatever `max-age` you send.

The `Age` header in the answer says how many seconds ago this API asked Altinn for the decision. It is
usually `0` when this call asked Altinn, and a little more when Altinn was slow to answer.

post.summary: Check whether a system user or person has access
post.description: Asks Altinn whether the system user (`systemuserId`) or person (`pid`) may perform `action` on `resourceId`, on behalf of the organisation `customerOrganizationNumber`. Send exactly one of `systemuserId` and `pid`.

parameters.name: Cache-Control
parameters.description: How old an answer you accept, as `max-age=<seconds>`. `max-age=0` or `no-cache` always asks Altinn. Without it, the server's default applies. See How fresh the answer is in the API description.

parameters.name: X-Request-ID
parameters.description: An id to find this call by in this API's logs. Up to 128 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`. Without it, or with any other value, this API makes a new one. Every response has the id in its `X-Request-Id` header.

200.description: Altinn answered. This includes answers that deny access, so check `permit`.

Age.description: How many seconds ago this API asked Altinn for the decision. Usually `0` when this call asked Altinn.

X-Request-ID.description: The id of this call in this API's logs: the `X-Request-Id` you sent, or a new one.

400.description: The request was not accepted. `type` says why.

X-Request-ID.description: The id of this call in this API's logs: the `X-Request-Id` you sent, or a new one.

value.title: A service this API depends on rejected the request

502.description: This API could not get a decision from Altinn. Your request did not cause it. Treat it as no access for now, and try again later.

X-Request-ID.description: The id of this call in this API's logs: the `X-Request-Id` you sent, or a new one.

value.title: A service this API depends on failed

503.description: The decision cache could not be read, and this API is set up to refuse calls rather than ask Altinn without it. Your request did not cause it. Treat it as no access, and try again later.

X-Request-ID.description: The id of this call in this API's logs: the `X-Request-Id` you sent, or a new one.

500.description: An unexpected error in this API. Treat it as no access.

X-Request-ID.description: The id of this call in this API's logs: the `X-Request-Id` you sent, or a new one.

systemuserId.description: The system user, when your caller uses one. In the Maskinporten token it is the UUID in `authorization_details[].systemuser_id`. Send either this or `pid`, not both.

pid.description: The person, when your caller is logged in as one: their national identity number or D number, from the `pid` claim in the Ansattporten token. It must have a valid date and check digits. In test, synthetic persons such as those from Tenor are accepted too. In production, only real persons are. Send either this or `systemuserId`, not both.

resourceId.description: Your resource's id in the Altinn Resource Registry, for example `altinn_access_management`. At least 4 characters, using lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. An id that does not exist is not rejected with a `400`. You get a `200` with `decision` `INDETERMINATE` instead.

customerOrganizationNumber.description:
The customer: the organisation the system user or person acts on behalf of when calling your API.

- For a system user, it is the org number in `authorization_details[].systemuser_org` in the
  Maskinporten token. Do not use the `consumer` claim. That is the vendor's own org number.
- For a person, it is the organisation they chose when logging in, in
  `authorization_details[].authorized_parties[].orgno` in the Ansattporten token.

Send the 9 digits without the `0192:` prefix: `311718371`, not `0192:311718371`. The last digit
must be a valid check digit.

action.description: What the caller wants to do, as named in your resource's policy, for example `read` or `write`. Any value that is not empty is accepted.

permit.description: `true` only when `decision` is `PERMIT`. Before granting access, also check `minimumAuthenticationLevel`.

decision.description:
Altinn's answer:

- `PERMIT`: allowed. Check `minimumAuthenticationLevel` before granting access.
- `NOT_APPLICABLE`: no rule gives access. This is the usual answer when the caller has no access.
- `DENY`: a rule refuses access.
- `INDETERMINATE`: Altinn could not answer, for example because `resourceId` does not exist. See
  `status`.

status.description:
Tells "no access" apart from "could not answer". Both come with `permit` `false`.

- `urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:status:ok`: Altinn evaluated the request.
- `urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:status:processing-error`: Altinn could not evaluate it, for example because
  `resourceId` does not exist. This points to a mistake in the request, not a refusal.

Not always present.

minimumAuthenticationLevel.description: The lowest level your end user must have logged in with for a `PERMIT` to hold. See Authentication level in the API description for how to find your user's level. Only present when Altinn sets such a requirement.

field.description: The request field or header, for example `customerOrganizationNumber` or `Cache-Control`.

code.description:
- `MISSING`: the field is absent, null or blank. If neither `systemuserId` nor `pid` is sent, both
  are listed.
- `INVALID_FORMAT`: the field is present but not valid.
- `CONFLICTING`: both `systemuserId` and `pid` were sent. Both are listed.

message.description: What is wrong, for people to read. The wording may change.

type.description:
What went wrong, as a name that does not change, so your code can rely on it.

- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:validation-error` (400): one or more fields are missing or invalid. `errors` lists all of
  them.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:malformed-request` (400): the request could not be read, for example a body that is not
  valid JSON, a field with the wrong type, or a `Content-Type` that is not `application/json`.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:upstream-rejected` (400): the values passed this API's checks, but Altinn rejected them.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:not-found` (404): there is no endpoint at this path.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:method-not-allowed` (405): the endpoint at this path does not accept this HTTP method.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:upstream-error` (502): this API could not get a decision from Altinn. Your request did
  not cause it.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:decision-cache-unavailable` (503): the decision cache could not be read, and this API is
  set up to refuse calls rather than ask Altinn without it. Your request did not cause it.
- `tag:kartverket.no,2026:internal-error` (500): an unexpected error in this API.

title.description: A short name for the `type`, the same every time.

status.description: The HTTP status code, the same as the response's.

detail.description: What went wrong this time, for people to read. Left out when `title` says it all. The wording may change, so check `type` in your code.

errors.description: Only with `tag:kartverket.no,2026:validation-error`: every field that failed, so you can fix them all at once.
